verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 3 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 1 advisory. REJECT.
acceptanceGrade: REJECT. The remasurement is half-performed. v3 correctly flipped the two measured booleans against live HEAD — file08CarriesG31 true, requiredNowUnchanged 28 — but carried v2's passProperty and failsIf across byte-identically without remeasuring them. Those two fields are exactly the fields that bind an executing runner, and they still assert the v2-era world: that file 08 does not carry G31, that a claim of G31 being live on file 08 is a failure, and that live required-now is 26. The artifact therefore contradicts its own header in the only places where the contradiction has operative force, and by its own failsIf[2] it fails. Everything else I attacked held: thirty-four cited path/digest pairs and eighteen recordedInputs entries all reproduce, the eleven classes match D-130 field-by-field and in order, no status token is recorded, no twelfth class, no G15 ride, no DR-104 SATISFY, no reopened leftover-design, and the subject did not move.

blockers.measurement: False at live HEAD aa19af2. File 08 carries DR-G31 IDENTITY-NAMESPACE-NEGATIVE-TEST-EXECUTION at docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md:367, placed there by D-167 on 2026-08-20, inside the file 08 revision the subject itself pins as f909ddff….
blockers.selfContradiction: The same artifact states file08CarriesG31 true, file08DoesNotCarryG31 false, registerRowNote "File 08 carries DR-G31 (D-167)", and authorityClaim "File 08 carries G31." The pass property asserts the negation of four of its own fields.
blockers.why: This is the dispatch's first named attack surviving into the one field a runner is bound by. passProperty is not commentary — it is the property an execution of this harness must satisfy. A runner reading it is told to measure against a register state that has not existed since D-167. The remasurement's whole purpose was to correct that state.
blockers.provenance: v3's passProperty is byte-identical to v2's. It was carried forward, not remeasured. At v2 the sentence was true (HEAD 5d5d778, file 08 3a9442d1, G31 absent); at v3 it is false.
blockers.consequence: Recording v3 would enter into the corpus a specification whose binding property denies a live register row. Any later act that cites v3's passProperty would unwrite D-167 by inheritance.
blockers.repair: Remeasure the sentence against live HEAD. It should read that file 08 carries G31 (D-167) and that the row is OPEN and not QUALIFIED — or the sentence should be dropped from passProperty, since register occupancy is not a property of an execution run.

blockers.claim: "G31 is claimed live on file 08" retained as a failure condition.
blockers.measurement: G31 is live on file 08. D-167 assigned the row and D-169 confirms the 28-member required-now set that contains it. The subject claims G31 live in authorityClaim, registerRowNote, file08CarriesG31, eligibilityEffect, and whatThisCloses.gates2and3HoldNote.
blockers.selfContradiction: The artifact satisfies its own failure condition. By failsIf[2] as written, this specification fails.
blockers.why: A failsIf list is the artifact's own refutation surface — the set of statements whose presence invalidates it. Leaving a v2-era refusal in place after the refused fact became true does not merely read oddly; it makes the artifact self-defeating on its face. An independent reviewer cannot ACCEPT a specification that fails its own stated test.
blockers.provenance: v3's failsIf is byte-identical to v2's, entry for entry. At v2 this entry was a correct guard against prematurely claiming a gate that did not exist. At v3 it guards against the truth.
blockers.consequence: Either the entry is dead text in a field that must be live — or it is live, and v3 is REJECT by its own construction. Neither reading permits recording.
blockers.repair: Invert or retire the entry. The live-world guard is the converse: G31 is claimed absent from file 08, or D-167 is unwritten.

blockers.measurement: Live required-now is 28, not 26. D-167: "Required-now becomes the prior 26-member set plus G31 (cardinality 27)." D-169: "Required-now becomes the prior 27-member set plus G32 (cardinality 28)." The dispatch and the review prompt both state 28. The subject's own requiredNowUnchanged field states 28, and doesNot[5] states "Does not change live required-now 28."
blockers.selfContradiction: failsIf[3] presupposes a 26 baseline that requiredNowUnchanged and doesNot[5] both contradict within the same file.
blockers.why: This is the dispatch's named attack "requiredNowUnchanged is not 28" landing in prose rather than in the integer. Reading failsIf[3] literally, correctly stating that live required-now is 28 — which is a change from 26 — is a failure of this specification. The guard fires on the true measurement and stays silent on the false one, which is the exact inversion of what a guard is for.
blockers.provenance: Carried byte-identically from v2, which was measured at required-now 26. Two coordinator decisions have moved the number since.
blockers.consequence: A later cycle honoring v3's failsIf would be told that the live cardinality is a defect. Combined with B1 this makes v3's binding fields a snapshot of a register state two decisions stale.
blockers.repair: Rebaseline to 28, matching requiredNowUnchanged and doesNot[5].

shouldFix.measurement: The live file 08 harness cell for DR-G31 reads "named: harness.DR-G31.identity-namespace-negative-test.preview (D-167; not authored; not QUALIFIED). eleven-class corpus (…)". The subject's string is v2's, byte-identical, and omits the "D-167; " attribution. The eleven-class parenthetical matches exactly; the divergence is precisely and only the provenance token.
shouldFix.why: At v2 this field was a proposal for a cell that did not exist, and omitting D-167 was correct because D-167 had not happened. At v3 the cell is live and carries the attribution. A field labelled Verbatim that does not equal the live cell it names mis-describes the register. Worse, if the proposal were ever applied as written it would strip D-167 from the cell — which the subject's own doesNot[21] forbids: "Does not unwrite D-167, D-175, or D-207."
shouldFix.consequence: Not a blocker on its own: the artifact does not edit file 08, so nothing is unwritten today. But it is the same v2-carryover defect as the three blockers, in a field whose name promises live fidelity.
shouldFix.repair: Either quote the live cell including "D-167; ", or rename the field to record it as the historical v2 proposal rather than a verbatim of the live cell.

advisories.detail: The subject's claimVerbatim is the live file 08 claim cell plus a trailing period the register cell does not carry. Every other character matches. Recorded for honesty, not as a finding — the register's cell text is unambiguous and no meaning turns on the period. Noted because the field name promises byte fidelity and, on this file, three other carried-forward fields did not deliver it.

rootCause.diagnosis: v3 is a partial remasurement. The header layer was remeasured against live HEAD and is correct; the binding layer was copied from v2 and is not.
rootCause.evidence: passProperty is byte-identical between v2 and v3. failsIf is byte-identical between v2 and v3, entry for entry, twenty-six entries. proposedHarnessCellVerbatim and claimVerbatim are byte-identical between v2 and v3. Meanwhile file08DoesNotCarryG31 flipped true→false, file08CarriesG31 was added, requiredNowUnchanged moved 26→28, head moved 5d5d778→aa19af2, and file08Pin moved 3a9442d1→f909ddff.
rootCause.why_it_matters: A remasurement artifact that copies its own pass and fail conditions forward has not remeasured — it has re-dated. The three blockers are not three independent slips; they are one omission with three visible faces, which is why fixing them individually without re-walking every carried field would be a band-aid. The correct repair is a field-by-field remeasurement of every string carried from v2, with the v2-era measurements either updated or explicitly marked historical the way basedOn.predecessorV2.role already correctly does.
